why: The design is settled and the brief writes the predicates, the two functions and the DO block (its vault secret, URL and guard match baseline_4 lines 66 to 115, and cron_jobs has the columns the upsert names). Commit 2 is a migration that replaces production's scheduler, and its cron block is skipped in PGlite and CI's Postgres, so no check runs the actual tick command. A typo in the net.http_post job, or a predicate copied narrower than its claim (the brief asks the model to compare six claims and use the code's), passes every test. Commit 1 changes queue claim logic in three runners with int tests and touches no money or permissions.
harm_if_wrong: After the deploy the nine routes would stop being called (or work would wait until the 15-minute sweep), stalling AI page jobs, cookie scans, theme photographs and the Dream Factory until someone writes a new migration, because production schedules must not be fixed by hand.
brief_problems: It depends on steps 0.23, 1.10, 1.22 and 1.26 (query-budget.int.test.ts, the cookie-scan due statement's new shape, the outside watcher, the tracked work wrappers), none of which exist yet; their shapes are assumed.

The scan case 'every cron route is reached' must parse `function commerce.cron_due` out of the newest migration and `format(call, '<name>')` out of the baseline; the brief gives the rule but not the parsing, which a cheap model may get loosely right and still pass.
